title: An early resistance warning helped doctors change a woman’s antibiotic
summary: China Medical University Hospital’s Intelligent Anti-Microbial System flagged ceftazidime resistance in 1 hour, and doctors changed a 78-year-old woman’s antibiotic before she recovered.
account: A 78-year-old woman at China Medical University Hospital developed severe pneumonia during a prolonged admission. The hospital says that the pneumonia began at the end of May 2022 and that she developed sepsis from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia on 2 June 2022. The hospital’s Intelligent Anti-Microbial System predicted within an hour that her Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolate resisted ceftazidime and suggested levofloxacin. Hospital clinicians said that conventional susceptibility testing takes two to three days. The clinicians changed the antibiotic in June. The hospital reported that she recovered and went home in late July 2022, weeks after the switch. The account concerns one patient. More than 100,000 platform uses and the projected changes in hospital mortality describe the wider service. Neither figure is a count of demonstrated recoveries. On 27 December 2022 the Ministry of Health and Welfare's Fengyuan Hospital signed a memorandum to adopt the platform. In a systematic review published on 30 September 2026, independent reviewers rated the hospital's own before-after study of the platform at serious risk of bias because it had no concurrent control group.
purpose: Help clinicians select an effective antibiotic sooner by predicting resistance from routine mass spectra.
system: 智抗菌平台 / Intelligent Anti-Microbial System (i.A.M.S)
developer: China Medical University Hospital, Taichung (team of superintendent Der-Yang Cho 周德陽, Po-Ren Hsueh 薛博仁 of the Department of Laboratory Medicine, and Jiaxin Yu 游家鑫)
domain: Healthcare - clinical microbiology and antibiotic therapy
segment: Hospital laboratory AI (antibiotic-resistance prediction from MALDI-TOF spectra)
taxonomy_note: The AI's part was turnaround time, a resistance prediction in one hour instead of days.

ratings.reason: The treating hospital described timely treatment of a severe infection, followed by recovery and discharge. The account does not establish a counterfactual life saved.

ai_role.statement: The platform analyzed a bacterial mass spectrum to predict resistance and suggest an alternative antibiotic. Clinicians selected and administered treatment. The hospital attributes earlier selection to the system, but the available account cannot isolate its effect on survival.

evidence.citation: Hueda-Zavaleta M, Flores-Palacios R, Bardales-Silva F, et al. AI-based clinical decision support systems for antibiotic therapy in common adult infections: a systematic review from development to clinical implementation. Frontiers in Digital Health 8:1944745, 30 September 2026. Six of the seven authors work in Peru and one works at Arkstone Medical Solutions in New York; none has a tie to China Medical University Hospital. They appraise the hospital's own before-after study of iAMS and rate its risk of bias as serious.
evidence.title: AI-based clinical decision support systems for antibiotic therapy in common adult infections: a systematic review from development to clinical implementation
evidence.quote: The before-after study (Ho 2024) ( 18 ) received a serious risk-of-bias rating on ROBINS-I because it lacked a concurrent control group and was susceptible to temporal confounding and co-interventions.

produced_by: The hospital's own laboratory identifies isolates by MALDI-TOF, so a spectrum exists as soon as a culture grows
A machine-learning classifier trained on the hospital's spectra and susceptibility records for Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and ceftazidime, one of nine species the platform covers
The platform returns the resistance prediction and a suggested alternative to the treating team within an hour
must_hold: The organism and antibiotic are ones the model was trained for
Clinicians act on the prediction before the conventional susceptibility result arrives
An effective alternative antibiotic is available and tolerated by the patient

echoes.setting: Tri-Service General Hospital, Taipei, a different team and system: a randomized trial of an AI decision support tool that predicts Stenotrophomonas maltophilia resistance from MALDI-TOF spectra one day early, across 1,600 infections. Fourteen-day mortality was 11.5 percent with the tool and 15.1 percent without it, with outcomes rated through unblinded clinician surveys (Lin et al., Implementation Science).

brief: A 78-year-old woman at China Medical University Hospital in Taichung developed severe pneumonia during a prolonged admission. The hospital's Intelligent Anti-Microbial System predicted within an hour, from a bacterial mass spectrum, that her Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolate resisted ceftazidime, and it suggested levofloxacin. Po-Ren Hsueh, a vice-superintendent of the hospital, said that conventional susceptibility testing takes two to three days.[1] Clinicians changed the antibiotic in June 2022, and the hospital reported that she recovered and went home in late July 2022.[2] The benefit rests on one patient, and every account of her comes from the hospital and its staff. In a paper published on 30 September 2026, researchers with no tie to the hospital rated the hospital's own before-after study of the platform at serious risk of bias because it had no concurrent control group.[3] The hospital's count of more than 100,000 platform uses describes the wider service and gives no number of recoveries.[4] The hospital's account supports an earlier change of antibiotic, and no source establishes that the prediction saved her life.

display.answer: Observed June 2022. The benefit is the switch of antibiotic after the platform flagged resistance. The hospital says that pneumonia set in at the end of May 2022, and a photo caption in the same release says that the patient developed sepsis from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia on 2 June 2022. The prediction and the switch followed that infection, so they came in June 2022. No source gives the day of the switch.

produced_by: The hospital's own laboratory identifies isolates by MALDI-TOF, so a spectrum exists as soon as a culture grows
A machine-learning classifier trained on the hospital's spectra and susceptibility records for Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and ceftazidime, one of nine species the platform covers
The platform returns the resistance prediction and a suggested alternative to the treating team within an hour
must_hold: The organism and antibiotic are ones the model was trained for
Clinicians act on the prediction before the conventional susceptibility result arrives
An effective alternative antibiotic is available and tolerated by the patient

echoes.setting: Tri-Service General Hospital, Taipei, a different team and system: a randomized trial of an AI decision support tool that predicts Stenotrophomonas maltophilia resistance from MALDI-TOF spectra one day early, across 1,600 infections. Fourteen-day mortality was 11.5 percent with the tool and 15.1 percent without it, with outcomes rated through unblinded clinician surveys (Lin et al., Implementation Science).
